Two ends, one loop.

the brand book

Two ends, one loop. The lemniscate's warm end (Ember) is the human act: the hand word, the key cable, the call to action. Its cool end (Signal, on the Midnight hue) is the structure: lines, diagrams, data. Midnight is the space they connect across.

IdeaMarkColourTypeGridShapeIconsMotionNode in 3D3D kitChannelsFormattingAssetsResearch
01 · Idea

Connection, drawn as one line

Infinite is a canvas where anything patches into anything. The mark is a single closed line with two ends of one colour field. Every surface uses those two ends and the space between them.

Ember, the warm end

The human act: the hand word, the key cable, the one call to action. Hue 38. One per frame, under 10% of its area.

Signal, the cool end

Structure: lines, diagrams, data, focus, selection. Hue 276, on the same hue as Midnight so it never fights the ground.

Midnight, the space

Every neutral sits on hue 274: Midnight grounds, Moon inks, Mist and Paper for reading. Never pure black or white.

Personality

calm, precise, a little playful, confident, never hype. The line: A DAW for you.

02 · Mark

A lemniscate of Bernoulli

Lemniscate of Bernoulli: x = A sin p / (1 + cos^2 p), y = A sin p cos p / (1 + cos^2 p), p in [0, 2 pi). The stroke is 87/338 of A, so the mark keeps its weight at every size. Draw it from the formula, never trace it.

stroke ratio87/338 of A
width2A + s = 2.2574 A
heightA / sqrt(2) + s = 0.9645 A
aspect2.341 : 1 with stroke (2 sqrt 2 : 1 for the centre line)
arc length5.2441 A (2 x lemniscate constant 2.62206)
crossingthe branches cross at 90 degrees, each at 45 degrees to the axis
clear space2 s on every side

On every ground

Midnight: default.

Mist: allowed.

Paper: allowed at 24 px and up (the light stops are soft on white).

Neverrecolour the stops, rotate, outline, add a glow or shadow to the flat mark, put it on a photo without a Midnight tile, or set it below 20 px wide (16 px for the tile icon).

Pixel 5x7drawn

Drawn, not a font file. Only when the machine itself speaks (prediction, learning).

05 · Grid

Grids per format

Web: 12 columns, max 1200, gutters 16/24/32, 8 px base. Film: 12 columns of 288 on a 3840 stage inside the 5% graphics-safe area. Social: 6% margins, 6 columns. Docs: A4, 18 mm margins, 4 pt baseline.

07 · Iconography

20 grid, 1.5 stroke, one dot

Keylines: circle 16, square 14, portrait 12×16, landscape 16×12, 2 px padding. Stroke 1.25 at 16, 1.5 at 20, 1.75 at 24. Corners 2 outside, 1 inside. The 3 px dot is the same dot as a pin.

Pair with words

An icon alone only for universal actions (play, stop, record, close). Everywhere else a label sits beside it.

One family

Line by default; the -fill variant shows the on state, never decoration.

08 · Motion

Springs you can measure

Overshoot = exp(-πζ/√(1-ζ²)). Settle (2%) ≈ 4/(ζω). For SwiftUI, response = 2π/ω and dampingFraction = ζ. For CSS, use the generated linear() curves in brand.css.

springζωovershootsettleSwiftUIuse
slab0.552012.6%292 ms0.314 s / 0.55Patch Type slabs, the key cable snap. The signature.
letter0.6229.5%271 ms0.286 s / 0.6Patch Type letters.
soft0.9180.2%262 ms0.349 s / 0.9Everything else that lands.
press1.0280.0%209 ms0.224 s / 1.0Buttons, keycaps, knob detents (no overshoot).

Grammar

verbwhat it means
LandAn object arrives and settles: soft spring, 4-8 u of travel, 200-320 ms. Slabs and the key cable use the slab spring.
PatchA cable draws from pin to pin: ease-out over 320-480 ms, plug snaps with the slab spring, the destination answers within 100 ms.
CarryBetween scenes an object travels and becomes the next frame (iris, zoom to a rect, carried object). No cuts on a beat that has motion.
LiveAnything that shows a value keeps moving: knobs breathe ±2°, waveforms scroll, meters fall. A frozen UI reads as a screenshot.
BreatheOne slow loop under everything (4-8 s): the ball's iridescence, the gradient sweep. Never on type, stops for reduced motion.

09 · The node in 3D

The node as an instrument

A node in 3D is a physical panel, like a pedal or a module, built from the app's own measurements. It is not a screenshot tilted in space. Reference: Audio Filter (src/app/bodies/FxBodies1.cpp, docs/plans/ui-system/element-sizes.md): body 440, readout strip 21, response viewer 190, row of 4 cells of 110 (type dropdown, freq, Q, gain), output row (mix, env).

Process

Capture

Start from the real node: its body in code (sizes from element-sizes.md and AppShared.h), a screenshot at 100%, the live values a user would set.

Lay out flat

Rebuild the panel as vectors in app pixels: cells, wells, captions, pins. The top view must match the app before anything gets depth.

Assign a z

Every component gets one height from the z table. Wells go down, prints stay flush, controls come up, caps sit highest. Nothing floats.

Give it a material

Matte body, satin knobs, glossy display, printed type. Colour comes from the mode roles; category colour only on the title strip, jacks and cables.

Light it once

Key upper-left behind (135°, 50°), rim upper-right behind, fill from the camera. Shadows always on and soft, contact shadow 0.25.

Frame it

3/4 view, yaw 20-30°, pitch 25-35°, 50 mm. One angle family per film; the camera sweeps sideways, it does not orbit.

Make it live

Knobs turn with the soft spring, keys press with the press spring, the viewer and meters keep moving, the key cable lands with the slab spring.

Check side by side

Put the render next to the app screenshot. Same order, same labels, same values. If a control is missing or added, it is wrong.

What went wrong in the film, and the rule now

r7 filmv2 rule
Flat textures skewed in 2.5D, so cards looked warpedReal geometry: an 18 u slab with a 3 u fillet, recessed wells, raised controls
Outlines on cards and controlsNo outlines: edges come from the fillet catching the key light
Win95 bevel blocks for buttonsPill keycaps on a shallow well: rest +6, pressed +2.5, LED for state
Dark cylinders for knobs, value arc floating in the airSkirt + knurled cap + engraved Moon pointer; the arc is printed on the panel at 1.12 r
Labels baked tiny into a textureCaptions are printed geometry in Geist, 13 u, at the app's caption gap of 4
No shadows, objects floated, no key lightOne key light, soft shadows on, contact shadow 0.25, ground in the mode colour
Glossy neon cables with big ball ends and glowMatte 5 u tubes, real plugs seated in side-wall jacks, catenary sag to the floor, no glow

Animation

partmotion
Knobturns with the soft spring; idle breath ±2°
Keycapdown 80 ms with press spring, up 140 ms; LED fades 160 ms
Switchthumb slides with the soft spring, track tints over 160 ms
Cabledraws pin to pin with ease-out, plug seats with the slab spring (12.6% overshoot)
Vieweralways live: curve and meters keep moving

12 · Formatting and voice

Plain and specific

rule
UnitsNumber, thin space, unit: 120 BPM, 4.00 ms, 1.20 kHz, -6.0 dB, 48 kHz / 24-bit
DatesISO in data and filenames (2026-10-10); 10 October 2026 in prose
Versionsv0.5.0 with the v; release names in sentence case
Node namesExactly as the app spells them, Title Case: Audio Filter, Color Ramp, Liquid Glass
KeysCmd/Ctrl + K, keycap chips in mono; macOS first, then Windows/Linux
Files and codeGeist Mono: tools/brand/build_3d.py, .inf, P.y += bass * 2
CaseSentence case for headings and buttons; lowercase for Patch Type slabs; mono caps only for folios
PunctuationNo em dashes, no exclamation marks, straight quotes in code, curly quotes in prose
SpellingBritish in prose (colour, centre); node and API names keep the app's spelling
NumbersTabular figures for values that change; minus sign for negatives in display type
Say

A frosted glass pane that bends what is behind it. Patch anything into anything. A DAW for you.

Never

“The world's first”, “revolutionary”, exclamation marks, em dashes, “free for now”, a second accent colour, a card with an outline.
